lessons.title: David (1): The youngest son
lessons.check_note: Shemot Rabbah 2:2 (Sefaria Midrash Rabbah 2022) and Megillah 14a read on Sefaria. English: JPS Tanakh Gender-Sensitive.

cards.title: Not the tall one
cards.body: God sends **Samuel** to the house of **Jesse** in Bethlehem to anoint a new king. Samuel sees the eldest son and is sure: this must be the one.

cards.q: In the Midrash, how did God test David before making him king?
choices: By how he shepherded his sheep
cards.why: He fed each animal **according to its ability**.

cards.gloss: "There is still the youngest" (16:11). He is out **tending the flock**.

cards.title: A shepherd for each
cards.body: God tested David **with sheep**. He let the small ones out first to graze the **soft grass**, then the old ones on the middling grass, then the strong ones on the tough grass. God said: "One who knows how to herd the flocks, each according to its ability, will come and herd My people."

cards.q: In Shemot Rabbah 2:2, what made David fit to lead Israel?
choices: He cared for each sheep according to its needs
cards.why: Leadership as **care for each one** by what they can bear.
wrong_why: The eldest looked strongest, and was passed over.

cards.gloss: "the horn of oil" (16:13). The Talmud notes that kings anointed from **a horn**, like David, kept their kingship, as Hannah's song foresaw.

cards.prompt: Samuel looked at height; God looked at the heart. What do people miss when they look at you, and what might you be missing in others?

points: Shemot Rabbah 2:2: tested by shepherding **each according to its ability**.

lessons.title: David (2): David and Goliath
lessons.check_note: Sotah 42b read on Sefaria 11/13 (its sexual readings of Goliath's mother omitted).

cards.title: Forty days
cards.body: The Philistine champion **Goliath** comes out every morning and evening, for forty days, and dares Israel to send a man to fight him.

cards.q: In the Talmud, Goliath came out morning and evening to stop Israel from saying the Sh'ma.

cards.title: Morning and evening
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan**: Goliath came out **morning and evening** to keep Israel from reciting the Sh'ma at its proper times. And his **forty days** match the forty days the Torah was given: he wanted to do away with it.

cards.q: According to Rabbi Yochanan, why did Goliath taunt Israel morning and evening?
choices: To stop them from saying the Sh'ma on time
Because the sun was in his eyes at noon
cards.why: The battle was also over **the Sh'ma**.

cards.body: The **Sh'ma**, said morning and evening, is what the Talmud says Goliath tried to stop.

cards.gloss: "but I come against you in the name of GOD of Hosts" (17:45).

cards.title: The one who kissed, the one who cleaved
cards.body: The Talmud identifies Goliath's mother with **Orpah**, Naomi's other daughter-in-law. **Rabbi Yitzchak**: God said, the children of the one who **kissed** Naomi goodbye will fall into the hands of the children of the one who **cleaved** to her. David descends from **Ruth**. **Rava**: for the four tears Orpah shed for her mother-in-law, she merited four mighty sons.

cards.q: In Sotah 42b, how are David and Goliath connected?
choices: David descends from Ruth, Goliath from Orpah

cards.title: His own words
cards.body: **Rabbi Meir**: three times Goliath's own mouth foretold his fall. He said "let him come down to me," placing himself below; he spoke of losing before he spoke of winning; and he asked, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with staves?"

cards.prompt: David faced Goliath with a sling and a Name. What giant are you facing with what you already have?

points: Sotah 42b: Goliath came morning and evening to stop **the Sh'ma**.
"**I come against you in the name of GOD**" (17:45).

lessons.title: David (3): That man is you
lessons.check_note: Avodah Zarah 4b-5a and Shabbat 56a read on Sefaria 11/13.

cards.title: A king who takes
cards.body: David takes **Bathsheba**, wife of Uriah, and arranges for Uriah to die in battle. Then God sends the prophet **Nathan**.

cards.q: According to the Talmud, what can any individual who has sinned learn from David?
choices: That kings are above the law
cards.why: Avodah Zarah 5a: go to David, and learn **that one can repent**.

cards.title: The poor man's lamb
cards.body: Nathan tells the king a story: a rich man with many flocks took a poor man's **only lamb**, which he had raised like a daughter, to feed a guest. David is furious: the rich man deserves to die.

cards.gloss: "I stand guilty before GOD!" (12:13). In Hebrew, **two words**.

cards.title: The teacher of repentance
cards.body: **Rabbi Yochanan** in the name of **Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai**: David was not the kind of person to do this, nor was Israel the kind of people to make the golden calf. It happened so that if **an individual** sins, he is told: go to David, and **learn that one can repent**; and if **a community** sins, go to the people of the calf. David's "last words" (II Samuel 23:1) are read as: David, who **raised up the yoke of repentance**.

cards.q: In Avodah Zarah 5a, why is David's story held up to an individual who sinned?
choices: To show that one can repent
To show that kings can do as they like

cards.title: Did David sin?
cards.body: Not every rabbi agreed. **Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani** in **Rabbi Yonatan's** name: "Anyone who says that David sinned with Bathsheba is nothing other than mistaken," reading that soldiers gave their wives a conditional divorce before battle. But **Rav** says David's one sin was **the matter of Uriah** (1 Kings 15:5), and Nathan's words in the text are plain.
Every Amidah opens with a verse from this psalm: אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח (Psalm 51:17).

cards.q: Which psalm's heading places it after Nathan confronted David?

cards.prompt: David's confession is two words. What makes them so hard to say?

points: "**I stand guilty before GOD**": two words (12:13).
Avodah Zarah 5a: David teaches **that one can repent**.
Shabbat 56a: some rabbis defend him; Rav does not.
Psalm 51: "**Fashion a pure heart for me**", and the Amidah's first words.

cards.title: Songs of a king
cards.body: David is a shepherd, a soldier, a king, and above all remembered as **a singer**.

cards.q: In the Talmud, a lyre over David's bed played by itself at midnight.
cards.why: The north wind came at midnight and played it (Berakhot 3b).

cards.gloss: "The favorite of the songs of Israel" (23:1).

cards.title: The lyre at midnight
cards.body: A **lyre** hung over David's bed. At midnight the **north wind** blew and it played by itself, and David rose and **studied Torah until dawn**. At dawn the Sages came: the people need food. David answered, "Go and sustain one another."

cards.q: In Berakhot 3b, how did David know it was midnight?
choices: The north wind played the lyre over his bed
cards.why: The wind **played the lyre**, and David rose.

cards.title: Five times, O my soul
cards.body: David says "Bless the Lord, O my soul" **five times**. One answer: once for each world he lived in, from his mother's womb to his last day. Another: the soul is like God in five ways. As God **fills the world**, the soul fills the body; God **sees and is not seen**, and so does the soul; God sustains the world, the soul the body; God is **pure**, the soul is pure; God dwells in **an innermost chamber**, and so does the soul. So let the soul praise God.

cards.q: In Berakhot 10a, why should the soul be the one to praise God?
choices: It shares five qualities with God
It is the oldest part of us
cards.why: Like praising like: **the soul** to **its source**.

cards.prompt: The Talmud says David sang a song for each stage of his life. What would your soul bless God for at this stage of yours?

points: "**The favorite of the songs of Israel**" (23:1).
Berakhot 3b: **the lyre at midnight**; "sustain one another."
Berakhot 10a: the soul is like God **in five ways**.
